title: Shared-year samples weaken the distinction between earlier and later runoff slope losses in two south-east Australian gauge sets
abstract: We tested whether the 2010-2021 loss of annual rain sensitivity differs clearly from the losses in 1959-1971 and 1983-1995. We reused signed CAMELS-AUS annual tables and fitted each gauge reference outside the earlier test window. We sampled shared year blocks and spatial cells, refitted the reference, and formed a direct paired contrast. Complete test records gave 21 and 33 mainland gauges. At block length three, 0 of eight contrast intervals were below zero, compared with 3 of eight in the wider available-year sets. The late slope alone was below zero in 5 of eight complete-record tests. Joint contrast limits were 1.8-5.7 times as wide as cell-only limits. Thus a late slope loss has stronger support than a unique late form. This does not prove equal forms or a recurring climate cause. Short periods, record selection, related rain products and uncertain small-sample interval coverage limit inference. The support rule was changed after pilot fits and is disclosed. Code, aggregate draws, source hashes and an independent scalar audit are included.

display.caption: Late-minus-early residual rain slope contrasts. Bars are 95% limits from joint spatial-cell and synchronous year-block samples. L is block length in years. The complete test-window sets have 21 and 33 mainland gauges. Zero is marked by the dashed line.

citations.reason: Tests the direct early-late slope contrast with shared-year and cell samples; support checks limit certainty without refuting the prior stationary null.
Verified annual flow, rain and gauge metadata.
